newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon says no qualms in welcoming China brass.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon says no qualms in welcoming China brass.

text.p: The Pentagon said on Tuesday it had no reservations about preparing a red-carpet welcome for Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian, who helped crush the 1989 pro-democracy protest in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.

"The answer to the question is 'No,'" Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon said when pressed on whether the Pentagon had any qualms about honouring someone involved in the use of force against democracy campaigners.

Chi, who was to arrive in the United States on Thursday for a 10-day fence-mending visit, was chief of the general staff during the June 4, 1989, Tiananmen massacre, in which hundreds of people were believed to have been killed.

The crackdown at Tiananmen sent U.S.-Sino relations into a tailspin from which they have never fully recovered. In recent weeks, however, U.S. and Chinese leaders have moved to improve ties with a visit to Beijing by Secretary of State Warren Christopher and talks between Chinese President Jiang Zemin and U.S. President Bill Clinton at a meeting of Asia-Pacific leaders in the Philippines last month.

Bacon said Defence Secretary William Perry, who received full military honours and "very fine treatment" during an official visit to Beijing in October 1994, planned to reciprocate to Chi, whose U.S. trip was postponed twice because of tension over Taiwan.

A brief U.S. government profile of Chi prepared for the visit made no mention of his role at Tiananmen Square. But a U.S. intelligence official, citing the "full intelligence record," said Chi was neither the architect nor the driving force behind the crackdown, which the official said was the work of political leaders.

Perry and Chi are to discuss bilateral military issues, as well as global and Asia-Pacific security matters, China's official Xinhua news agency has said. The Pentagon said it would spell out his itinerary at a briefing on Thursday.
